correctness.rationale: This PASS is for repairs/4/RESULT.md and the corresponding verification notes, not the original stock-law wording. Independent atomless utilities need not give uniform orders. Independent U_j uniform on (2j,2j+1) are strictly ordered by index, so there is never a successful triple and T is infinite, contradicting the original Finding under its stated independence-and-atomlessness condition. The repaired Finding and scope require i.i.d. atomless utilities, which by symmetry give uniform prefix rankings and a coherent no-ties order almost surely. For any selected triple, envy-free assignments necessarily give its extremes to agents 1 and 2, so the third must prefer its middle to both. Giving the third her top choice on any triple and arranging the others as in the repaired proof leaves at most one ordered envy pair, simultaneously optimizing the three objectives if no envy-free triple exists. Absence of a middle-first triple is inherited after deleting a favorite endpoint and forces every deletion to be at an endpoint; conversely the middle cannot be the first deleted member of a triple. For the stated process the monotone no-success tail is 2^(m−1)/m! for m>=2 and 1 for m=0,1. Differencing gives the mass; using weights 1 and 2m+1 on the tail gives the two moments (e²+1)/2 and (5e²+1)/2, hence the stated variance. The linear-time witness uses the maximum (worst numeric rank) on each side, so it tests exactly the two strict comparisons. The unchanged checker was inspected, not executed; its exhaustive finite permutation cases do not imply sampling uniformity.

originality.rationale: For the repaired claim, credit the known single-dipped obstruction and the exact count of endpoint orders. Neither that obstruction nor the known interval-prefix permutation count gives the full conditional allocation classification for arbitrary third rankings and the common optimum for the three envy objectives. That deterministic classification with a constructive bound is the supported distinct contribution. The uniform stock law is retained as a corollary of it and a known count, not as an independently novel pattern-enumeration result. The adjacent indexed stock law randomizes all three agents and is not the same conditional law.
residual_risks: An equivalent polarized allocation theorem or conditional law could be unindexed. The original Simion–Schmidt full text was not obtained, so no specific negative claim is made about it. Known pattern enumeration is not part of the originality pass.

value.rationale: The fixed-opposite-orders input is a natural extreme of disagreement. The structural result replaces general allocation search by a direct witness test and determines three different ordinal envy objectives, including the existence of a common optimizer. The explicit stock distribution under coherent uniform prefixes interprets the criterion probabilistically, without pretending the known permutation count is itself a contribution. The repaired model excludes the concrete nonidentical-utility counterexample to the frozen wording.
